items.title: Baidu releases ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview open weights under Apache 2.0: 280B-total, 14B-active MoE with 1M context
items.summary: Baidu published weights for the first post-trained checkpoint of ERNIE 5.5 Flash, a 280B MoE that activates 14B per token, with a 1M-token context, FP8 weights with FP4 experts, and a built-in DSpark draft head for speculative decoding. It targets coding, agent and knowledge work and is still mid post-training. vLLM (via a plugin) and SGLang had day-0 serving; SGLang reports single-request decode raised from 102 to 1,074 tok/s on 4 Blackwell GPUs.

doubt.pushback: Baidu itself calls it an intermediate post-training checkpoint; one replier notes it is text-only with no image input. Benchmarks so far are Baidu's own.

reception.summary: Mostly short congratulations and excitement about open weights and 1M context; one asks for image input, a few compare its size to DeepSeek; no hands-on results yet.

items.title: Tencent open-sources Hy-MT3 translation models (1.8B, 7B, 30B-A3B) covering 102 languages
items.summary: Tencent released the third generation of its Hy translation family under Apache 2.0, in 1.8B, 7B and 30B-A3B MoE sizes with FP8 and GGUF builds, expanding from 38 to 102 languages. Tencent reports 43% fewer mistranslations and 74% fewer omissions than Hy-MT2 on real-world data, and the 30B-A3B tops its non-thinking comparison; it also released the TransRubric evaluation and a paper.

doubt.pushback: A replier asks why TranslateGemma-27B is missing from the comparison and whether direct non-English pairs were tested; results are Tencent's own.

reception.summary: Replies welcome the jump to 102 languages and game localization; questions about OpenRouter availability and missing baselines; nobody reports trying it yet.

items.title: Strata v0.2.21 makes Inkling 2 Mini up to 3x faster on long prompts across NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and DGX Spark
items.summary: The open-source Strata local inference app shipped 0.2.21: on an RTX 4090 Inkling 2 Mini decodes at 92 tok/s after a 32K prompt (was 29), an RTX 3060 Ti 8 GB goes from 11 to 43 tok/s, prompt reading on M5 Max is 62% faster and DGX Spark gains 12 to 58%. Agent sessions now reuse their prompt cache on every backend, and the DSpark drafter works with Unsloth GGUFs.

items.title: TensorFold fork drafts all streams' next tokens in one shared pass, lifting Inkling 2 Mini from 284 to 372 tok/s at 16 streams on a Mac Studio
items.summary: A builder's fork of the TensorFold Apple-silicon engine batches speculative drafting across 16 concurrent streams, raising total throughput about 31% while each stream's output matches running it alone token for token.

items.title: Independent rebuild of NVIDIA's CPU-ARC cached-reasoning replay on one RTX 5090 finds it does not hold, failing most on familiar-looking questions
items.summary: A builder reimplemented the CPU-ARC idea, where a CPU replays a large model's cached reasoning instead of running the model, and reports the cache trails the 27B model on new maths questions and breaks worst on questions that resemble cached ones. A useful negative replication for anyone planning cache-based CPU offload.

doubt.pushback: Single-person replication on one GPU; method details are in the post and video only, no code linked.

items.title: Community tiny-voca TTS ports (4.5M to 27M params) reach #1 for Hindi and Arabic on the Hugging Face Open TTS Leaderboard
items.summary: Community fine-tunes of the tiny-voca text-to-speech models now rank first for Hindi and Arabic and top four in Turkish, Greek, French and Russian on Hugging Face's open TTS leaderboard, showing tiny on-device TTS can compete across languages.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco open-source Shirudo, an eBPF runtime where agents write signed temporary shields for running Linux systems
items.summary: Shirudo lets operators (and agents such as Codex) build signed eBPF or Java micropatches that block a vulnerable code path on a running Linux host without a restart, with TPM-backed attestation. OpenAI reports a Codex-written shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit on live Elasticsearch in a controlled test. Pre-release; production needs Shirudo kernel patches and TPM 2.0. BSD-2-Clause.

doubt.pushback: Repliers ask how agent-written rules are scoped, expired and rolled back, and how to prove a shield will not drop legitimate traffic; the only result so far is a vendor-run controlled test.

reception.summary: Security practitioners welcome the patch-gap framing and eBPF approach; the main questions are review gates before load, rollback and blast radius.
